features.name: any_comment_formal_citation_syntax
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment contain formal citation syntax (numbered bracket reference, markdown hyperlink, or author-year parenthetical)?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments with json.loads into a list of strings; missing/malformed -> null; empty list -> 0. For each comment test regex (case-insensitive) r'\[\d{1,3}\]|\]\(\s*https?://[^)]+\)|\([A-Z][A-Za-z\-]+(?: et al\.?| and [A-Z][A-Za-z\-]+| & [A-Z][A-Za-z\-]+)?,? \(?(?:19|20)\d{2}[a-z]?\)?\)|\bet al\.'. Return 1 if any comment matches, else 0. Purely mechanical on raw text; no semantic filtering.

h1: Rows with any_comment_formal_citation_syntax=1 have higher delta rates than rows with 0.
note: Operational assumption: "formal citation syntax" is defined as a fixed regex set (numbered brackets, markdown links, author-year parentheticals, et al.); it is not exhaustive and bare URLs are excluded. Persuasiveness is measured via delta at the row level, as an association only. Comments are unordered and unscored; the row-level any-flag cannot tell which comment persuaded the OP. Raw comment text may contain outcome announcements; no semantic filtering applied. Rows have at most a few comments and comment timing is unknown.
